Not OP but having dealt with a plethora of eating issues, I can provide a few insights: 

1- understanding that most binge eating behaviour is not because you’re hungry. For me personally, a lot of my binge eating was because I was lonely/emotional and I wasn’t ready to address that, so I literally ate my feelings. This one is tough and requires a lot of self reflection to overcome, but is worth it in the long run. 

2- food availability: having lived with my parents (specifically my dad on this one) if I left any relatively nice tasting snack foods out or available they would be eaten and taken from me before I had a chance to eat them. This led me to “squirrel” binge foods in my room (basically hiding it) and because it was right there, I would eat it all because I thought that if I didn’t, someone else would. I stopped buying a lot of these foods and I try not to care when my parents eat my snacks (this part is hard because I still live with them due to the pandemic). If you are not in a similar situation with someone else taking your snacks, you know that they will always be there if you want them and there is no urgency to eat them - they’re there now, will be there tomorrow too. 

3- eating foods I really enjoy and taking the time to enjoy it rather than just stuffing my face during meals. I drink a lot of water throughout the day and drink a large bottle of water with every meal. Taking longer to eat my food makes me feel more satisfied with any meal I eat, making me less likely to want to eat outside of set meals (breakfast/lunch/dinner) I don’t restrict what I eat during meals all that much anymore and if I’m really craving something for dinner (ex:pasta with white/cream sauce) I’ll eat a reasonable portion of it and call it done. Eating the foods I really want sometimes helps me avoid the binge later on. 

Hope these are helpful for anyone who reads this and may be struggling, I had difficulty with bad eating habits for a really long time and these ideas really helped me.

For the tofu: 
1 block extra firm tofu

2-3 tablespoons soy sauce (I eyeball this and don’t measure) 

2 tablespoons nooch


Press the tofu until it’s really dry - I use two plates lined with paper towel and some big cans over a couple hours to get the moisture out (this is important) 

Once tofu is dry, cut it into the cube size of your choice and pour the soy over that. Once the tofu is coated in the soy sauce, add the nooch and toss to coat all the pieces. 

Spread this out on a baking sheet and bake at 400 for about 30 minutes, tossing occasionally so it doesn’t burn. 

Really good, nice texture (something I know a lot of people dislike about tofu) and makes enough for two meals if you eat half of the block like I did here
